# Rights and attribution

The numerical research results originate in the chapter by Çiler Hatipoğlu, Elżbieta Gajek, Nihada Delibegović Džanić and Lina Milosevska (2022), [DOI 10.14705/rpnet.2022.61.1451](https://doi.org/10.14705/rpnet.2022.61.1451), pp. 154–161, Research-publishing.net.

The live UIST record and publisher-deposited Crossref metadata identify the chapter licence as [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Its first page names the authors and states CC BY. The appended colophon describes the whole book as CC BY-NC-ND and explicitly states that individual articles can have different licences. This extraction relies on the chapter-specific licence; it does not relicense the book or appended colophon.

The package retains that attribution and licence link for the reused chapter material. Changes are: selecting published percentage indicators, transcribing values to CSV, paraphrasing labels, adding source-page and period context, and writing new documentation. This is a derived compilation, not an original-author-issued data release. No endorsement by the source authors is claimed.

Use of CC BY material requires appropriate credit, a licence link and an indication of changes, without suggesting endorsement. Other rights can still apply. The licence does not give access to unpublished respondent data or substitute for depositor authority, ethics or privacy decisions.

Before repository deposit, the responsible compiler must confirm the deposit agreement and the reuse licence for their own contributions. CC BY 4.0 is the proposed package licence. No repository-wide policy has been used to relicense existing material.
